problems.stem: $\lim_{x \to 2} \dfrac{x^2-4}{x^2+4}$ is

problems.stem: $\lim_{x \to \infty} \dfrac{4-x^2}{x^2-1}$ is
problems.explanation: Use the Rational Function Theorem: the degrees of the numerator and denominator are the same (both 2), so the limit is the ratio of leading coefficients, $\dfrac{-1}{1} = -1$.

problems.stem: $\lim_{x \to 3} \dfrac{x-3}{x^2-2x-3}$ is

problems.stem: $\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{x}{x}$ is

problems.stem: $\lim_{x \to 2} \dfrac{x^3-8}{x^2-4}$ is
problems.explanation: Note that $\dfrac{x^3-8}{x^2-4}=\dfrac{(x-2)(x^2+2x+4)}{(x-2)(x+2)}$. Canceling $x-2$ and substituting $x=2$ gives $\dfrac{4+4+4}{2+2}=\dfrac{12}{4}=3$.

problems.stem: $\lim_{x \to \infty} \dfrac{4-x^2}{4x^2-x-2}$ is
problems.explanation: Use the Rational Function Theorem. The degree of the numerator and the degree of the denominator are equal (both 2), so the limit is the ratio of leading coefficients, $\dfrac{-1}{4}$.

problems.stem: $\lim_{x \to -\infty} \dfrac{5x^3+27}{20x^2+10x+9}$ is
problems.explanation: Use the Rational Function Theorem. The degree of the numerator (3) is greater than the degree of the denominator (2), and the ratio of leading coefficients $\dfrac{5}{20}>0$, so as $x \to -\infty$ the quotient behaves like $\dfrac{x}{4} \to -\infty$.

problems.stem: $\lim_{x \to \infty} \dfrac{3x^2+27}{x^3-27}$ is
problems.explanation: Use the Rational Function Theorem. The degree of the numerator (2) is less than the degree of the denominator (3), so the limit is 0.

problems.stem: $\lim_{x \to \infty} \dfrac{2^{-x}}{2^{x}}$ is
problems.explanation: The fraction is equivalent to $\dfrac{1}{2^{2x}}$; as $x \to \infty$ the denominator $\to \infty$, so the limit is 0.

problems.stem: $\lim_{x \to -\infty} \dfrac{2^{-x}}{2^{x}}$ is
problems.explanation: Since $\dfrac{2^{-x}}{2^x}=2^{-2x}$, as $x \to -\infty$, $-2x \to \infty$, so the fraction $\to +\infty$.

problems.stem: $\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\sin 5x}{x}$
problems.explanation: $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sin 5x}{x} = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sin 5x}{x}\cdot\dfrac{5}{5} = 5\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sin 5x}{5x} = 5(1) = 5$.

The line $y = 2$ is a horizontal asymptote.
problems.explanation: Since $2+7x-4x^2 = (2-x)(1+4x)$, both $x=2$ and $x=-\dfrac{1}{4}$ are vertical asymptotes. Also, since the numerator and denominator have equal degree with leading coefficients $2$ and $-4$, $y=-\dfrac{1}{2}$ is a horizontal asymptote.

problems.stem: Let $$f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{x^2-1}{x-1} & \text{if } x\neq 1 \\[4pt] 4 & \text{if } x=1\end{cases}$$ Which of the following statements is (are) true? I. $\lim_{x \to 1} f(x)$ exists. II. $f(1)$ exists. III. $f$ is continuous at $x = 1$.
problems.explanation: Since $f(x)=x+1$ if $x\neq 1$, $\lim_{x \to 1} f(x)$ exists and equals 2. So I is true. $f(1)=4$ is defined, so II is true. But $2 \neq 4$, so $f$ is not continuous at $x=1$; III is false.

problems.stem: If $$f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{x^2-x}{2x} & \text{for } x\neq 0 \\[4pt] k & \text{for } x=0\end{cases}$$ and if $f$ is continuous at $x = 0$, then $k =$

problems.stem: Suppose $$f(x)=\dfrac{3x(x-1)}{x^2-3x+2} \text{ for } x \neq 1, 2, \qquad f(1) = -3, \qquad f(2) = 4.$$ Then $f(x)$ is continuous

But $\lim_{x \to 2} f(x)$ does not exist (the denominator $\to 0$ while the numerator $\to 6$), so $f$ is not continuous at $x=2$, regardless of the value assigned to $f(2)$.

problems.stem: The graph of $y = \dfrac{2x^2+2x+3}{4x^2-4x}$ has

problems.stem: Questions B5\textendash B9 refer to the function $f$ defined on $[-1,3]$ by $$f(x)=\begin{cases}1-x & -1 \le x < 0 \\[2pt]2x^2-2 & 0 \le x \le 1 \\[2pt]-x+2 & 1 < x < 2 \\[2pt]1 & x = 2 \\[2pt]2x-4 & 2 < x \le 3\end{cases}$$ The function $f$ has a jump discontinuity at

problems.stem: $\lim_{x \to 0} \sqrt{3+\arctan\dfrac{1}{x}}$

As $x \to 0^+$, $\dfrac{1}{x}\to \infty$, so $\arctan\dfrac{1}{x}\to \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, giving $y \to \sqrt{3+\dfrac{\pi}{2}}$. Since the one-sided limits are different, the limit does not exist. problems.stem: Questions B13\textendash B15 refer to the graph of a function $f$ on $-3 \le x \le 3$, described as follows.
